en.title: From comparing four cards to reading two together

sources.label: Waite · Part III §5: recurrence in dealing, upright and reversed lists

en.bodyMarkdown:
The four cards laid out for this article were chosen to make a comparison possible. All four share a number because we selected them that way. That is different from noticing two or more Fours among the cards actually dealt for a reading; the teaching arrangement tells you nothing about how unusual a shuffled result would be.

Waite offers a separate historical layer in [Part III, §5, on recurrence in dealing](https://sacred-texts.com/book/the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot/section-5-the-recurrence-of-cards-in-dealing). In his upright list, four Fours point to a journey near at hand, while three Fours point to a subject for reflection. He also prints a separate reversed list. These are divinatory associations, not measured frequencies or demonstrated probabilities. The table supplies no rule for a mixture of upright and reversed cards. Here “Fours” refers to the four suit cards, not every card bearing the numeral IV. Our exercise below develops the pictures and positions rather than adopting that recurrence table.

**Original hypothetical follow-on.** The reading group above has six members and a room confirmed for next month. The cost of materials for additional members is not yet known. Jun asks, “What can we build on, and what needs a limit before we invite more people?” For a paper exercise, deliberately place the Four of Wands upright in “an existing resource” and the Four of Pentacles upright in “a boundary to examine.” These two positions and cards are our teaching choices, not an actual draw or a traditional fixed combination.

The Four of Wands can focus attention on the usable arrangement already in place; the Four of Pentacles can prompt a closer look at the resources that must last. This applies Waite’s associations of harmony and holding on to possessions to this invented situation. It does not establish that the group is happy, that the budget is inadequate, or that its treasurer is possessive. An available room and an unresolved cost can exist together; the two cards need not cancel each other out.

1. **Keep both jobs visible.** Write what supports the group beside the first position and what needs a limit beside the second. “Both mean stability” leaves those two questions unanswered.
2. **Join them with a condition.** Try “We can keep the meeting arrangement, provided we check what a larger group would need.” The condition is a proposed planning question, not a guarantee supplied by the cards.
3. **Choose one check.** List the extra materials required for a small increase in membership, find their actual cost, and compare it with the funds the group has agreed it can use. Then decide whether to expand, keep the present size, or seek a different arrangement.

Suppose materials are already covered by a sponsor, but the room’s capacity is unknown. Then the practical question shifts to confirming capacity with the venue. Do not keep inventing a money problem to defend the Four of Pentacles interpretation. Known facts can change the application while the original question, positions and card record stay visible.

After the paper comparison, try the [tarot table](/tarot) with the cards actually drawn. Free table permits a custom layout; it does not promise these two cards or assign our resource/boundary labels for you. Record your chosen positions separately. For the individual images, return to [Four of Wands](/journal/tarot-four-of-wands) and [Four of Pentacles](/journal/tarot-four-of-pentacles), then explain what each contributes to this particular question.

zh.title: 从四张并排比较，走到两张一起读

sources.label: 韦特第三部第5节：发牌中的重复，正位与逆位词表

zh.bodyMarkdown:
本文桌面上的四张牌，是为了比较而主动挑出来的。四张数字相同，是选牌方式决定的；这与一次实际发牌后发现两张或更多“四”不同。教学摆法不能告诉你，某种洗牌结果究竟有多罕见。

韦特在[第三部第5节“发牌中牌张的重复”](https://sacred-texts.com/book/the-pictorial-key-to-the-tarot/section-5-the-recurrence-of-cards-in-dealing)另列了一层历史读法：正位表里，四张“四”对应近期旅程，三张“四”对应值得思考的事；他还另列逆位表。这些是占卜联想，不是测得的频率或经过验证的概率，表中也没有说明正逆混合时怎样计数。这里的“四”指四种花色中的四号小牌，不能把所有带有 IV 的牌都算进去。下面的练习从图像与牌位出发，并不采用那张重复词表。

**原创假设续例。** 延续上面的读书会：现有六位成员，下个月的房间已经确认，新增成员所需的材料费用还不清楚。小钧问：“邀请更多人之前，我们能依靠什么，又该先设哪条边界？”在纸上练习时，主动把权杖四正位放在“已有资源”，星币四正位放在“需要检查的边界”。两个牌位与牌张都是本站的教学选择，不是实际抽牌，也不是传统规定的固定组合。

权杖四可以把注意力引向已经可用的安排；星币四则提醒检查哪些资源需要维持。这是把韦特关于和谐、守住已有资源的联想，应用到这段假设情境，不证明成员都很开心、预算一定不够，或管账的人有占有欲。房间可用与费用未明可以同时存在，两张牌不必互相抵消。

1. **保留两个任务。** 在第一位旁写下什么支持读书会，在第二位旁写下什么需要边界。只说“两张都是稳定”，还没有回答这两个问题。
2. **用条件连起来。** 可以试写：“我们可以保留现在的聚会安排，前提是先查清扩大人数需要什么。”这条条件是提出的规划问题，不是牌给出的保证。
3. **选一项核对。** 列出小幅增加成员需要补充的材料，查实际费用，再与大家同意可使用的经费比较，然后决定扩大、维持人数，还是寻找别的安排。

假设材料已经有赞助，未知的却是房间容量，实际问题就应转向向场地方确认人数限制。不要为了维护星币四的解释，一直编造经费问题。已知事实可以改变具体应用，同时把原问题、牌位与牌张记录保留下来。

纸上比较后，可以到[塔罗牌桌](/tarot?locale=zh)练习实际抽到的牌。自由桌面允许自订布局，却不保证发出这两张牌，也不会替你设定这里的资源／边界标签；请另外记下自己选的牌位。需要核对单牌图像时，回看[权杖四](/journal/tarot-four-of-wands?locale=zh)与[星币四](/journal/tarot-four-of-pentacles?locale=zh)，再说明各自怎样回答这一次的问题。
